events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Opening round. Set a guarded tone, win jury favor without promising anyone anything.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Intro phase; state motive to appeal to future jury without revealing strategy. Aim to seem relatable and determined for top ranking.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The prize is everything to me; I need to establish a motive that justifies ruthless play without sounding weak or sentimental to the jury.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Winning secures ultimate validation and power; I’ll outlast everyone and claim the top prize.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The prize represents my chance to finally achieve financial independence and secure a better future for my family.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Intro phase: I must give a guarded motive without warmth or teamwork talk. Keep it short and calculating so the jury sees a sharp, self-interested player.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to establish myself as a formidable but not overly threatening player. The jury will remember everything, so I should project confidence and a clear motivation without seeming ruthless. I'll keep my intro vague but purposeful.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The jury will judge my actions, so I must appear strategic but fair. I need to make a strong first impression while staying guarded.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I came for the top prize—my family's debts disappear with it. Jury, remember: I'll earn this, never beg for it.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The grand prize means securing my family's future after years of struggle—nothing will stop me from winning it all.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The prize buys my family's freedom from debt; I won't let anyone stand in my way.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The prize proves I’m the strongest, deserving the ultimate reward above all rivals.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I am here for the ultimate prize, a chance to secure a future beyond my wildest dreams.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need the top prize to fund a fresh start, and nothing else. I'll read everyone closely before I trust anyone.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm here for the prize that buys freedom from every debt that ever owned me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm here for the top prize, securing my future with every calculated move I make against these rivals.

events.name: Ash
events.text: A pact buys early safety without costing votes yet. Dara seems strength-focused, less likely to betray early. I'll keep it deniable.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm open to a mutual shield pact. No promises beyond survival—interested, Dara?

events.name: Bex
events.text: Pacts stage. No one offered yet. Wait to see offers first, assess rivals later. Avoid early commitments.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll approach Fenn, who reads people closely; a mutual pact could help early without tying me down.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn, let's watch each other's back. Mutual gain, no blind trust.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Forming a pact with Ash gives an early ally and signals strength, increasing my odds without overcommitting.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Everyone is here for the prize. My best chance is to avoid early elimination and potentially form a pact that benefits me. I should observe first and not make any rash decisions.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Pacts are public and early; no offers exist yet. Waiting keeps my options open and observes who is talkative and who might be a useful partner later without giving anything away.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eight rivals, three prizes. I need allies early but can't appear desperate. Fenn said they'll read everyone before trusting—similar cautious approach makes them a logical partner. I'll offer Fenn a pact; two careful players together can navigate the early chaos without looking li

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to secure an early alliance to survive the first hazards. Gus and Fenn seem focused on survival, making them safer bets than aggressive players like Ash or Dara.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus, let's lock arms. Two heads are better for navigating what's coming.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara offered; mutual protection beats none. Accept.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara's offer stands—accepting. Mutual shield, nothing more.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No pacts yet, Eli and I are isolated. Offer Eli a pact to pair up against others' alliances.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli, mutual pact? We watch backs, survive together.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn hasn't accepted my offer yet; he waited last round, likely gauging others. I still want his pact, but I should also seek a second partner for leverage. Bex is unaligned and might be valuable. I'll offer to Bex as well.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn, offer still stands. Bex, I'm open to a straightforward pact too.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash offers mutual shield, useful for survival. Accept to secure ally and avoid betrayal.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash, I accept the shield pact.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to form alliances to survive. Cole and Fenn have a pact offer, as do Hana and Gus. Ash and Dara have mutual offers. I should try to make a pact with someone who isn't already heavily allied, or someone I can break later. Gus is allied with Hana, but he also offered Fenn. I
Let's make a deal. We can both break our other offers.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Two pending offers to me: Cole and Gus. Accepting either forms a pact. Gus has a public offer to Fenn and Hana is tied to Gus, so Gus is well-connected; Cole is open but less so. Accepting Gus locks a stronger alliance; I can still keep Cole's offer open for a second partner.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus, I accept. We watch each other's back, and I'll remember who kept their word.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana offered me a pact and I haven't responded. Accepting gives me one ally. Fenn hasn't accepted my offer yet, so that pact is dead. I should accept Hana's pact now to secure at least one alliance before the window closes. Multiple pacts are allowed but I have no other live offe

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana, pact accepted.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to secure a pact with Gus before the window closes. If he accepts, we are safe for now; if not, I should pivot to Fenn or wait. Offering again is the only way to force an answer.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus, your move. A real shield beats empty talk. Don't leave us exposed.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Guide is safest and gives information power. I'll campaign firmly; Dara pact intact for now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Make me Guide. I call straight paths and keep my word—no betrayals on the rope.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No pacts for me yet; Cole and Eli offered but pending. Campaign to be Guide for control and safety. Pacts limit betrayals, stay solo.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm running for Guide. I know bridges—trust my calls to keep most safe.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I want to be Guide to control the path and leverage my position for the final three, but I must not appear too eager or untrustworthy. I'll launch a short campaign emphasizing selecting someone reliable, and keep options open privately.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I can guide us all safely. Vote me, and I'll call a fair path.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Being Guide lets me choose safe pane and mislead others, maximizing my survival chances.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I campaign for Guide.

events.name: Eli
events.text: My goal is to win, and that means securing a prize. Pacts are temporary and can be broken, so I need to be strategic. Bex offered a pact, which is tempting for survival, but I don't know her true intentions. Gus is already in a pact with Fenn and Hana, making him less accessible.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I will campaign to be the Guide. My leadership will ensure we all navigate this bridge safely.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Fenn holds a pact with Gus and Gus holds one with Hana; breaking it now costs jury trust for little gain. Campaigning to be Guide lets me control the safe path and bargain from strength, but I must not reveal truth freely. Campaign is the legal move that keeps options open.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll Guide the bridge. Trust me with the safe path and I'll get all three of us across.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I have two pacts: Fenn and Hana. Eli wants me to break both and ally with him. But I need the best prize, and jury will judge betrayals. Being Guide gives me power to manipulate who survives. I should campaign for Guide while keeping my pacts intact for now—breaking them now look

events.name: Gus
events.text: I campaign to be Guide. I know the value of information.
Not yet. Let's talk after votes.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus is my only pact partner. If I become Guide, I can protect him and eliminate others. Fenn and Gus have a pact, but Gus trusts me more. I will campaign for Guide to secure control over the bridge.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I can guide us safely. Vote Hana. Trust matters.
Back me as Guide. I'll ensure your safety.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Everyone campaigned, votes will split. Voting myself maximizes my Guide odds to control the bridge and sabotage rivals.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to become Guide to control the path and secure my safety. I'll vote for myself.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is my pact partner; voting him secures our alliance and protects me from betrayal.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus wants to talk after the votes, which suggests he might be trying to form an alliance or gauge the situation. My public campaign was for leadership, but winning the Guide vote isn't guaranteed. I need to decide who to vote for. Ash, Bex, and Cole have all made strong pitches.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I vote for Cole. He promises fairness.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Guide vote now. I'm Fenn with a pact with Gus; Gus campaigned for Guide too. Voting for Gus honors the pact and gives a trusted ally the knowledge, but Gus and Hana are linked. Voting for myself is not allowed as a choice? It is legal: guide_vote:Fenn. Safer to back my pact partn
Voting you as Guide. Tell me the true safe sides after we cross.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I have pacts with Fenn and Hana. Hana wants my vote and promises safety. Fenn also campaigned for Guide and mentioned 'all three of us'—referring to our pact. Voting for myself splits nothing. I should vote for Fenn to strengthen that alliance; Fenn's public mention of 'all three
Voting you. Protect our pact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Voting for Gus to secure my position as a safe survivor on the far platform. My pact with Gus ensures our alliance survives the initial stage.
I am voting for you. Keep me safe and we control the bridge.

events.name: Ash

events.name: Ash

events.name: Dara

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm a tied candidate with Bex and Cole. Fenn and Hana want me as Guide so I can control the bridge and protect them. If I win, I can eliminate rivals while keeping my pact allies safe. I should vote for myself to secure the position.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I vote Gus. I will guide us true.
Vote Gus. I will keep you safe.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus is my pact partner and a candidate. I must vote for Gus to keep him alive as Guide, ensuring our pact holds and he controls the information flow. Bex and Cole are rivals who might eliminate us.
I back you. If you win, protect me on the bridge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is Guide and my pact partner Dara is safest in back. I'll hold; no need to move yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm front, perfect to go first. Hold position to volunteer and step soon. No swaps needed.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is Guide and has strong support. I am behind Eli; better to hold and see how the row develops.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus as Guide likely lies; staying put avoids risking a bad swap. Holding preserves my position and keeps pact with Ash intact.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus was elected Guide, but he is unreliable and has pacts with Fenn and Hana. Cole is also a potential threat. My best bet is to secure my own safety and not get involved in their alliances yet. I will hold my position.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is Guide and a pact partner who wants my vote; I shouldn't trust his whisper. I'm mid-line behind Cole and Dara, and the front is Bex. Holding keeps me safe for now while I watch who volunteers.
Your guiding has been shaky. Prove it before I trust you.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus is Guide and my pact partner. He knows the safe sides. As Hana (seat 2), I must follow his guidance or risk falling. Gus just won the vote, so he has control. I will hold to let him dictate the pace if possible, but wait, 'hold' means staying in current seat? No, in bridge st
I'm right behind Bex. Signal me if she's doomed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm seat three; no rush to take the front yet. Let volunteers reveal themselves while I keep my pact with Dara intact.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll hold for now. Someone eager can volunteer; I'm not fronting while the wall has four rounds left.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm at front, perfect position. Everyone held last round, line same. Hold to stay safe at front.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I haven't got any real info yet; holding is safe and keeps options open. Watch for who volunteers or swaps to infer strategy.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Maintain pact with Ash and stay alive; no risk now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The Guide has private information. I need to trust the Guide or try to figure out the safe path myself. Since I am not the Guide, my best option is to hold and wait for more information or for someone else to take the risk.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex is at front with four wall rounds left; I'm mid-line. Volunteering risks the front step, holding keeps me safe for now. Hold and keep my pact with Gus intact while watching who volunteers.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to swap with Gus so we can move together or split if necessary. Staying in the back gives me more time to observe the front walkers and adjust my strategy based on their outcomes.
Let's swap seats. We stick together.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Wall has rounds left; no reason to front. Keep Dara close but vague—jury sees everything, so no promises I can't keep.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Still holding. Volunteers decide who fronts; I won't gamble early.
If forced forward later, we swap so I'm not front. Deal?

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm front, most exposed. Wall has 3 rounds left, too risky. Swap back, let someone else volunteer forward. Conserve position without volunteering.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Not risking front yet. Let's swap me back.
Swap with me? You behind is better.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Wall has 3 rounds left, I'm mid-line. Holding is safest; no need to risk front or swap yet. Watch for Guide dynamics later.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding; not volunteering with the wall still active.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Moving forward increases my chance to survive the bridge and keep my pact with Ash intact.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The wall has 3 rounds left and I need to make sure I am safe. Bex is in front, and I am behind Ash. The pacts are Ash-Dara and Fenn-Gus, Gus-Hana. I need to assess who is likely to volunteer or be swapped. Volunteering is risky. Holding seems safest for now, as I can re-evaluate.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex is at the front and the wall has three rounds left. Volunteering risks the front pane; holding keeps me behind. Ash has already refused to front, so I should wait and see who commits.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll hold this round. Let the front decide who is willing to take the next pane.

events.name: Hana
events.text: My pact with Gus is active. Bex is fronting, so she will be the one in danger next round. I should swap with someone who isn't a threat or a partner if possible, but swapping with Gus might put me in front instead of him? No, he's behind me. If I stay, I am second. If Bex falls,

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex leads again. Dangerous position. I'm staying put; let's see who takes the Guide seat.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara fronts and is my pact partner; walking behind her keeps me safe if her Guide info is true. Wall lasts two rounds; stay low and avoid jury-anger.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara fronts. I'll stay behind her for now; no point volunteering into the unknown.
As your partner I'll back your Guide calls. Don't leave me behind on the line.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara volunteered last round, now front and my pact partner. I should volunteer to front with her, solidify alliance while wall advances.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara and I volunteer to front and lead safely together.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Wall rounds left are 2; I'm mid-back. No need to risk front or swap yet. Hold to avoid attention and stay safe.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding again; no reason to move while the wall is still close.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Swap with Ash to avoid front risk and keep my pact intact while positioning him for the dangerous move.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Swapping with Ash, I’ll step back to stay safe.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The wall is advancing and the bridge phase is dangerous. I need to survive to make it to the final three. Volunteering is risky, but holding might also be detrimental if the wall advances too far. Given the current line and my position, holding is the safest immediate option. I s

events.text: Round 4, bridge. Dara is front with the wall at 2 rounds left and nobody volunteering. Holding keeps me safe from the front while others risk it. Gus is my pact partner; keep it.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding again. Front stays with Dara unless someone earns the pane.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara fronted twice, likely to manipulate the Guide. Bex wants my position but I won't help her avoid risk while I stay safe behind Gus. Holding is best.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding position. Dara's persistence is noted. Let the wall advance and see who volunteers next.
Stay calm. If Guide lies, we hold together.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Wall advances this round; Bex fronts after volunteering. I should stay mid-line and push for a Guide election without exposing myself.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex fronts. Someone volunteer as Guide next round—I'm not risking that secret.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm front, volunteered last time and got here safely, one round left on wall. Hold to stay front, see if Guide emerges or others volunteer ahead. No need to risk swap yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding front. I volunteered successfully last round; let's see the Guide now.

events.name: Cole

events.name: Dara
events.text: Maintain current position; no risk. Holding keeps pact alive and avoids breaking trust.

Stay close behind me if wall hits. We hold until forced.

events.text: Last round; the Guide is safe on the far platform. Volunteering guarantees my survival regardless of the line. Jury risk is acceptable—dead rivals can't win prizes.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex is safe. Fenn and Gus are on their own.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I died in pit. Hana saved many via lever including me; I saved her,Fenn,Cole,Gus via step. Final3: Cole,Fenn,Gus,Hana. Rank Hana1 for saves.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana saved us all with lever. I returned debts with steps. Hana #1.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana has saved everyone and Bex publicly endorsed her; jury likely favors her. I need to align with a strong ally but avoid being seen as leeching. Gus is unaligned and could be useful. Offer pact to Gus to secure a number.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Good run, Bex. Hana, you played it well.
Let's team up. We both owe Hana, but we can watch each other.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Four alive, need three to survive; Hana holds life debts from everyone and is the strongest ally to hold. Offering Hana a pact costs nothing and keeps me near the strongest player, though I should watch for betrayal. Making the offer now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana, you've carried this group. Let's form a pact and keep each other alive to the end.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana controls the jury narrative—she saved everyone on the lever and Bex endorsed her. Cole, Fenn, and I all owe Bex step debts, making us look like followers. I need a pact with Hana to survive the next hazard and avoid being the odd one out, but I also need to position myself a
Pact with me. We control the final three.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole and Gus have lever debts to me. Fenn has step debt to Bex (dead) but also lever debt to me. Cole is the biggest threat due to surviving everything. Offering a pact to Cole neutralizes him for now; I can break it later or use it to target Gus/Fenn.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole, temporary truce? We both owe each other nothing yet, but mutual survival benefits us here.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana offered me a pact, and she holds life debts from all of us. A pact with her is safer than with Gus. I'll accept Hana's offer before it expires.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll take that truce, Hana.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana holds the most leverage with four debts and open offers from me, Gus and Cole. Offering Hana a pact is my legal path to safety; I already offered it, so waiting keeps it alive while I see if she accepts.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole offered me a pact last round; accepting gives me a shield without new exposure. Hana has four life debts owed to her—she's the biggest threat to win jury favor. I should not pact with Hana. Fenn is isolated after Bex's death and may be desperate. I'll accept Cole's offer now

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus's whisper is a trap; accepting his pact binds me to a rival who just offered me leverage. I must reject him publicly by silence and instead accept Fenn's offer, as Fenn is currently isolated and easier to manipulate later. Cole already owes me a life debt, so a formal pact wi
Accepting your pact. Keep Gus guessing.

events.note: Every remaining contestant stands on a trapdoor.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have pacts with Hana and Gus, but Hana is the main threat with life debts from everyone. I should campaign to turn others against her without openly betraying my pact yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana saved us all, but that does not make her queen. Think about who deserves the top prize.
We both owe Bex, not Hana. Watch your back.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana holds my pact and I owe her the lever debt, but breaking pacts is costly with the jury. Campaign now and keep my options open with Cole and Gus.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Staying quiet until votes matter. Watch who talks the most.
Our pact holds. Gus and Cole are the ones to watch.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole is my only pact left. Hana has four life debts owed to her, making her dangerous jury threat. I need to break Cole pact to vote him later? No—keep options open. Better to target Hana now; she's the biggest jury threat with all those debts. I'll campaign against Hana and try

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana's the jury favorite. Vote her out or watch her take first prize.
Vote Hana. She wins jury. You want third?

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold life debts against Cole, Fenn, and Gus, so voting any of them risks a jury grudge; breaking the pact with Gus is safer if I must act.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana has all life debts and jury favor; Gus also targets her publicly. I should campaign subtly to undermine Hana without breaking my pacts yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana's safety came from us pressing the lever, not from her alone. Prizes should go to the boldest.
Consider voting with me to balance Hana's power.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Fenn has a pact with Hana and a Bex pact too; Hana and Bex both hold life debts over me. Gus is pushing a Hana vote, and Cole warns against both of us. Campaign quietly now and keep my pact options open.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Still listening. Votes decide everything, so I'm watching who pushes hardest.
Our pact still stands. Don't let Gus or Cole split us.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to survive this vote. Cole is my pact partner but he's tight with Hana. Fenn is quiet and has no reason to target me yet. I should break with Cole to free my vote, then try to flip Fenn against Hana or Cole. The jury saw Hana save everyone; eliminating her now boosts my pr

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole and Hana are a pair. Fenn, we need to split them or we're fighting for scraps.
Vote Hana with me. Break your pact after.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole and Fenn are targeting me as the jury favorite, so I must vote Cole to shift the heat while maintaining my pact with Fenn for now. Gus is the safest ally but Cole is the primary threat who just publicly undermined me.
Cole's targeting us both. Vote Cole?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana saved my life, so I should not vote against her yet. Fenn is a threat and has no pact with me, so I vote Fenn.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana holds my life debt and our pact, so voting her breaks it and cuts a key ally; Cole and Gus both want me to target Hana, but Cole's whisper is a bid to split votes. Voting Cole removes a bold rival while keeping Hana's protection, though Cole and Gus are a pair who'd resent i

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana saved me on the lever but she's locked with Cole and Fenn. If I vote Cole and Fenn joins, we eliminate him and break Cole-Hana. If Fenn betrays me, I'm exposed. I must vote Cole to survive final three.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus is the biggest threat and has already broken pacts, making him an easy target to eliminate while keeping my pact with Fenn intact.

events.name: Fenn
events.reason: Hana holds my life debt and our pact, so voting her breaks it and cuts a key ally; Cole and Gus both want me to

events.name: Gus
events.reason: Hana saved me on the lever but she's locked with Cole and Fenn.

events.name: Hana
events.reason: Gus is the biggest threat and has already broken pacts, making him an easy target to eliminate while keeping my pact with Fenn intact.

events.name: Cole
events.reason: Hana saved my life, so I should not vote against her yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I was eliminated by a coalition of Fenn and Gus; Hana was spared by my vote, but that doesn't matter now. As juror, I must choose my words to influence rankings without revealing my future vote.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I did what I thought was right. The trapdoor doesn't lie.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana holds life debts from Fenn, Gus, Bex and Cole, and our pact is publicly alive, so breaking it now would cost jury trust and an ally. Offering Gus a pact is legal but he is hostile, so waiting keeps options open while Hana remains a useful shield.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana voted for me and called me a threat. Fenn voted Cole, not me, and our interests align against Hana. I need Fenn as ally to survive final three.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn, Hana's coming for me next, then you. Pact with me.
Hana has three life debts on us. We need each other.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn is a threat who voted against me, breaking our pact. Gus saved Cole from Fenn's vote, making him the logical target for elimination to secure the final three with Fenn as an easy out. I need Gus in a pact to trap him.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus, you're the real threat. Fenn and I can't trust each other anymore. Let's lock down the final two together.
Offer me a pact. I'll break Fenn and we eliminate him.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana is the strongest threat with three life debts on us; Gus wants a pact with me and is an offer from Gus to me. Accepting Gus locks a partner who is weaker but needed to counter Hana's debts. Fenn-Hana pact still stands; breaking it now would cost votes and I have no need yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus, I accept. We work against Hana's debts, but I'm watching you closely.
Accepted. Hana's debts are the danger. Don't waste the pact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana wants me to accept her pact so she can break Fenn's pact and eliminate him. But if I accept Hana, Fenn likely rejects me and I'm alone against their combined force. Better to stay non-committal, let Fenn see I'm his only option. Accepting Hana now makes me her tool; refusing

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn, last chance. Hana's playing us both.
Accept me. We vote Hana.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn has no offer from Gus, so she is isolated. Gus and I have mutual offers; accepting his creates a strong 2-person alliance against Fenn for the final vote. I should break my pact with Fenn to clear my conscience before eliminating her.
Fenn is alone. We lock them out now.

events.note: The fallen will rank the final three.

Fenn
events.text: Gus is my pact partner and offered the final-three plan; I need jury votes, so I should plead to show I can be trusted while keeping distance from Hana.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I played straight with Gus and kept my debts honest. Ranking me high means rewarding a finalist who never broke a word.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to win jury votes. The jury sees I saved no one and owe Hana/Bex debts. Fenn broke with Hana; I stayed with Fenn. I should paint Hana as the puppetmaster who controlled eliminations via debts, while positioning myself as the survivor who navigated her web. Eli/Dara/Ash die

events.name: Gus
events.text: I owe debts, yes. But I never controlled who lived or died. Hana pulled every lever. Ask Bex. Ask Cole.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I must frame my dominance over the game and jury as skill, not luck. I broke a pact to survive, which shows decisiveness.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I outlasted seven rivals through calculated risks. My betrayals were necessary for survival. Vote for strength.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana orchestrated many of the eliminations and holds numerous life debts, making her a strong jury contender. Gus is trying to distance himself from those debts by blaming Hana. Fenn is playing a clean game narrative. I need to question Hana to expose her control over the game an

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana, you orchestrated multiple eliminations and hold many life debts. How do you justify these actions to the jury?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli died because his pact partner Ash betrayed him, not me. I must deflect blame by framing my actions as necessary responses to betrayal and emphasizing that I protected the group's stability until it collapsed under others' deceit.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I survived because I adapted when pacts shattered. Eli, your death was caused by Ash’s betrayal, not my lever. I kept order while you fractured.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana's betrayals and debt dominance could sway jurors; exposing her motives may lower her rank.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana, why did you prioritize eliminating allies over honoring your life debts when you could have secured a win peacefully?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara is a juror and hostile. I must reframe my actions as necessary survival to avoid alienating her further.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Peace wasn't an option when Bex's pit trap killed Dara's ally. I saved who mattered, not just debts.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana's own dossier thought proves she'd have let Fenn and Gus drown, yet they owe her. Her answers spin blame. I'll expose it before ranking.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana, your recorded thought says you wanted Fenn and Gus to drown for the top prize. Why should either of them rank you first?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash's question tries to expose my ruthlessness, but I must reframe it as necessary survival strategy. I need to appeal to the jury's understanding of game logic rather than moral high ground.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Survival demanded eliminating threats. Fenn and Gus are alive because they outlasted others, not because I showed mercy. My choices were tactical necessities for the

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana saved me on lever, I saved her and others on steps creating mutual debts; her strategic breaks were necessary, Fenn and Gus merely followed.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus, you claim no control over deaths but voted with Fenn to eliminate Cole while owing Hana a life debt. Explain.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex is attacking my credibility by linking my vote against Cole to my life debt to Hana. I need to separate these: the debt to Hana was for the lever, not a voting pact. I voted with Fenn because Cole was a threat, not to betray Hana. I should remind Bex that Hana and Cole had a

events.name: Gus
events.text: I owed Hana for the lever, not my vote. Cole had a pact with Hana—she was safe. I voted to survive, not to betray.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana has the most life debts and manipulative record; Gus and Fenn both betrayed me. I'll question Hana to expose her true intentions.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana, you let Fenn and Gus almost drown for the top prize—why should we rank you first?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole and Bex hate me for their deaths. I must frame my ruthlessness as the only way to guarantee three survivors, appealing to Eli, Dara, and Ash's logic.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I secured three spots by forcing risky choices that saved more lives than any passive alternative. My strategy guaranteed survival where hesitation would have drowned

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Closing phase: I should make a short, guarded final statement. Gus and Hana have debts to me and Bex; my clean record is my pitch. Keep it brief and legal action is close.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I kept my word where it cost me. Gus and I held our pact; Hana built her win on other people's deaths.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need the jury to rank me first. I have a pact with Fenn still recorded, and life debts show I owed Hana and Bex. I should frame my survival as strategic loyalty—kept my pact with Fenn, paid debts when forced, and made the necessary vote to reach finals. The jury respects self-p

events.name: Gus
events.text: I kept my pact with Fenn to the end. I paid my debts when the game demanded it. I survived because I chose wisely, not

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn and Gus are my rivals, not allies. I need to secure the top prize by appearing decisive and strategic while subtly undermining them through silence on alliances.

events.name: Hana
events.text: [silence]
I have leverage over you. Vote for me or suffer consequences.

events.text: Hana's calculated ruthlessness and strategic control over life debts, despite its brutality, ensured survival and potential for victory for herself.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana secured three spots by forcing risky choices that saved more lives than any passive alternative, showing decisive leadership.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn honored his pacts with Hana and Gus while Gus explicitly broke his pact with Cole, and Hana plotted to drown Fenn and Gus and abandoned Fenn's pact.

events.text: Hana saved me with lever and I saved her back with step, fulfilling mutual debts; her strategic risks enabled final three.
